EOG.thesis: Low-cost US producer at a forward P/E of 8.7 with strong free cash flow; Stage 2, Minervini 6/7, holding the 146.58 support (6 touches) just under its 50-day average 150.08. Thesis intact but momentum is fading with oil.
EOG.invalidation: A daily close below 141.5 (between the 146.58 and 139.39 supports) or WTI below $80 on an Iran deal.
catalysts: US decision on new Iran strikes

JNJ.thesis: Low-beta pharma and medtech cash flows with a dividend; Stage 2, Minervini 7/7, at 270.47 above the 264.78 support (6 touches) and its 50-day average 267.43.
JNJ.invalidation: A daily close below 252 (fails 264.78 and approaches 249.81).

PGR.thesis: Short rates heading toward 4.5% boost float income and auto pricing keeps pace with claims; forward P/E 14.4, Stage 2, Minervini 6/7, holding up in the sell-off at 231.39 below the 237.69 resistance (8 touches).
PGR.invalidation: A daily close below 213 (loses the 215.25 support) or a sharp rise in loss ratios.

MCK.thesis: The largest US drug distributor grows with GLP-1 and specialty volumes without taking drug-pricing risk; Stage 2, Minervini 6/7, forward P/E 20.4, at 1069 above the 1039.94 support. Buy a pullback to that support.
MCK.invalidation: A daily close below 990 (about 2 ATR under the 1039.94 support).
catalysts: Q3 FY27 results late January (date n/a)

LLY.thesis: Obesity-drug volume growth gives cycle-independent earnings; Stage 2, Minervini 7/7 at 1347 (RSI 50), 6% above its rising 50-day average 1265.59. Wait for a pullback toward the 1220-1250 zone.
LLY.invalidation: A daily close below 1125 (under the 1134.87 support) or a GLP-1 pricing shock.
catalysts: Drug-pricing oversight from the new Congress (January)

WMT.thesis: The largest beneficiary of consumer trade-down with grocery share gains and growing ad income; at 127.95 just under the 129.85 resistance and well above its 50-day average 116.65. Buy a pullback to the 122.0 support (4 touches).
WMT.invalidation: A daily close below 115.5 (under the 116.87 support and the 200-day average 118.68).
catalysts: Q4 FY27 results in February (date n/a)

CME.thesis: Futures volumes rise with volatility and rate uncertainty (VIX 36, Fed hiking); Stage 2, Minervini 6/7, at 307.56 on the 307.28 support. Buy a pullback toward the 289.89 support and the 50-day average 289.43.
CME.invalidation: A daily close below 280 (under the 289.89 support and the 50-day average).
catalysts: Monthly volume reports early December (date n/a)

XLP.thesis: Staples are the leading group (+10.2pp vs SPY over 1 month, +13.5pp over 3 months) as investors rotate out of AI; Stage 2, Minervini 6/7, at 90.46. Buy a pullback to the 88.63 support (5 touches).
XLP.invalidation: A daily close below 85.5 (under the 85.97 support, 7 touches).

outlook.regime: Overheat with an AI de-rating: firm growth and labor, sticky inflation (core PCE 3.1%, PPI 6.5%) and a Fed hiking into 2027, while the AI/semiconductor complex unwinds and the S&P 500 enters correction
outlook.summary: Since Nov 12 the macro regime is unchanged (overheat, Dec 9 hike priced ~97-100%, futures near 4.5% by mid-2027), but the market regime turned: SPY fell into correction (-11% from its record), QQQ closed 0.7 above its -20% line and SMH lost 24% in a month as AI payback doubts spread from Nvidia to memory, Broadcom and the Anthropic IPO. Defensive leadership is now the clear trend (staples +10pp, health care +7pp vs SPY over 1 month), oil fell to $84-90 on growth fears, and credit is softening (HY ETF at a 3-month low). The portfolio stays defensive: energy, quality health care, higher-for-longer financials and defensive consumer; LMT is removed after closing below its invalidation, and CME, MCK and XLP are added to the watch list.
drivers: Fed funds futures: Dec 9 hike fully priced, about 4.5% by mid-2027; Cook warns delay risks 'getting behind the curve'
10Y 4.91% after a -24bp haven rally in 5 days, still +78bp over 1 year; 10Y real yield 2.88% (98th pct)
AI de-rating: SMH -23.6% over 1 month, NVDA -13.7% on Nov 20; Nasdaq erased its 2026 gain
Defensive rotation: staples +10.2pp, real estate +9.6pp, utilities +9.3pp vs SPY over 1 month
Oil: WTI 83.8, Brent 90.1, -16% to -20% in a month despite Iran strikes being weighed; OPEC+ Nov 29
Credit: HY ETF 76.35 (3-month low), HY spread 3.52pp (86th pct)

themes.name: Energy supply squeeze
themes.why: Hormuz attacks continue and Trump is weighing new Iran strikes; a low-cost producer earns well even at $85-90 Brent, but the growth scare has pushed oil to 3-month lows.

themes.name: Quality health care
themes.why: Cycle-independent earnings and the leading defensive group (XLV +7.5pp vs SPY over 1 month, +26pp over 6 months); distributors avoid drug-pricing risk.

themes.name: Higher-for-longer financials
themes.why: A Fed hiking into 2027 lifts insurer float income; exchanges earn more from record volatility and rate hedging (VIX 36, MOVE 96).

themes.name: Defensive consumer compounder
themes.why: Consumer sentiment near record lows (UMich 51.5) pushes trade-down to discount retail; staples lead SPY by 10pp over 1 month.

risks: A violent AI/growth rebound from extreme fear leaves the defensive portfolio lagging
Credit deleveraging spreads to all sectors, including defensives and financials
A hot October PCE (Nov 25) or 50bp December hike re-rates high-P/E defensives (WMT 39.6x, KO/XLP)
An Iran deal or OPEC+ supply increase sends WTI below $80 and breaks the energy theme
Drug-pricing policy or CMS rules hit health care
